text:
Jamal - CSM: Hey team — quick sync request. Redpine's renewal is in ~6 weeks and procurement asked for a customer-facing SLO acceptance packet (uptime, p95 latency, and credit calc). Can we do a dry-run of the pack this week?
Aisha - CS Ops: Yep. I started a draft of the packet last night — includes uptime history + proposed credit table. Need engineering to confirm p95 targets and the evidence artifact we can hand them.
Sam - Eng: ping. What's Redpine's environment? Are they on Hosted or Dedicated? That changes the acceptable SLOs.
Jamal - CSM: They're on Hosted API, but they use a dedicated model pin (redwood-v2-small). Traffic profile: lots of short chat requests + some embeddings bursts.
Nate - Solutions Eng: For hosted with pinned model, our historical p95 for that model on eu-west looks like ~180ms for short requests, 350ms for mixed. I can produce the 90-day histogram.
Aisha - CS Ops: Awesome. Can you also export the KV cache hit rates? We want to show how caching reduces observed latency during peak.
Sam - Eng: Will do. Also want to confirm our SLO language: uptime = 99.95% monthly, p95 latency <= 300ms for <512 tokens. If we keep 300ms in the packet, legal will want the credit table spelled out.
Olivia - Legal: FYI I'll need exact wording for failure modes (region vs model vs full platform) and the credit computation formula. Keep it simple: credit = SLA% shortfall * monthly invoice capped at 50%. Example calc included.
Jamal - CSM: Olivia — can you validate the sample wording once we have the numbers? We'll do a dry-run with Redpine success manager.
deploy-bot: New export job completed: `exports/redpine/90d_latency_histogram.csv` (s3://redwood-exports/redpine/90d_latency_histogram.csv)
Nate - Solutions Eng: Uploaded cache metrics and token distribution to the same bucket: `s3://redwood-exports/redpine/cache_and_token_mix.json`
Aisha - CS Ops: Draft packet link: https://docs.redwood.com/packets/redpine-slo-acceptance-dryrun (edit access to CS + Eng + Legal)
Sam - Eng: Quick note — during a regional outage last month we routed traffic and p95 spiked to ~1.2s for ~18 minutes. Should we include that as an exception (force majeure) or a platform incident example?
Olivia - Legal: Include it as an incident example. We'll call out 'regional service disruption' as an excluded event for uptime credits, and include a note about mitigation steps + postmortem link.
Jamal - CSM: OK. Aisha, can you assemble the final one-pager with: 1) requested SLOs, 2) historical evidence, 3) credit table example, 4) exceptions and incident link, 5) customer acceptance checkbox?
Aisha - CS Ops: On it. I'll produce v0.1 by EOD tomorrow. Will add a short version for procurement and a longer technical appendix for their infra team.
Nate - Solutions Eng: For the credit calc example, use this sample snippet so procurement can reproduce:```
monthly_invoice = 12000.00
measured_uptime = 99.80
promised_uptime = 99.95
shortfall = promised_uptime - measured_uptime # 0.15
credit_pct = min(shortfall / promised_uptime, 0.5) # capped at 50%
credit_amount = monthly_invoice * credit_pct
```
Sam - Eng: LGTM. I'll add a note about p95 measurement window (5-minute moving windows aggregated hourly) so numbers are consistent.
Olivia - Legal: Once v0.1 is in, I'll do a short pass and add the formal contract clause language. Also recommend a single sentence clarifying that quantization/hosting config changes by the customer can affect latency SLOs.
Jamal - CSM: Perfect. After v0.1, I'll run it by the Redpine AM and book a 30-min review with procurement. If they sign off, we fold it into the renewal pack. :thumbsup:
Aisha - CS Ops: FYI I'll capture feedback in the packet as comments and a short changelog so we can iterate. Also capturing enablement items for the success manager (talking points, slide).
Sam - Eng: Anything I should add to the tech appendix? I can include: model pin behavior, fallback model routing, and KV cache TTLs.
Nate - Solutions Eng: Add a short blurb on how batching policy affects cost/latency tradeoffs — helps procurement understand unit economics.
Jamal - CSM: Great. Thanks everyone — estimate: v0.1 tomorrow EOD, legal pass next day, customer dry-run within 4 business days.
Aisha - CS Ops: Noted. I'll ping again once the draft is ready.
Olivia - Legal: I'll be available for a quick review after lunch tomorrow.
Jamal - CSM: Closing loop — action items: Aisha (assemble packet), Sam/Nate (provide metrics + appendix), Olivia (legal wording). tagging @Aisha - CS Ops @Sam - Eng @Olivia - Legal :white_check_mark:
